title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening for Private deployments
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Enforce KMS region pinning for RBAC v2 and strengthen audit logging for Private installer; no customer-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private need stronger guarantees that encryption keys and KMS usage are region-scoped to meet data residency requirements. Existing RBAC v2 allowed KMS keys to be referenced without explicit region checks; operators requested a hardening and observability improvements (ENG-3245 / SEC-1120).

Summary: This PR adds enforcement for KMS region pinning in the RBAC v2 policy enforcer and enriches audit logs with KMS-specific fields. The feature is configurable with an operator-visible mode (audit | enforce) and ships with a conservative rollout plan for Private deployments.

Key changes:
- Add region residency checks to the RBAC v2 policy enforcer. Policies referencing a kms_key must now include a kms_region attribute or pass the configured residency check. The enforcer supports two modes: audit (log-only) and enforce (deny).
- Enrich audit logs with kms_region, kms_key_id, policy_decision and policy_rule_id to aid forensic and compliance workflows. Audit entries are emitted to the existing audit pipeline (auditd -> log-indexer).
- Private installer: add a helm values flag privateInstaller.rbacV2.kmsResidency.mode (audit|enforce) and privateInstaller.rbacV2.kmsResidency.backfill=true to optionally run a migration to detect non-compliant keys during upgrade.
- Add integration tests for RBAC v2 KMS residency checks and audit log assertions.
- Doc updates: security and private-deploy sections documenting the configuration and migration steps.

Migration and rollout:
- Default behavior for existing Private installations is audit mode to avoid accidental denials. We recommend enabling the backfill detection and running the provided script to enumerate non-compliant keys. After validation, operators can flip to enforce mode during a maintenance window.
- Hosted customers are unaffected by default; enforcement is gated behind a Private-only config flag.

Testing:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation and log enrichment included.
- Integration tests run against the Private installer e2e harness.
- Performed staged rollout on internal staging clusters and a canary Private install.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing public API shapes. It does add a small config surface for operators and long-lived audit fields. Follow-up tasks: telemetry dashboard for KMS residency violations and automatic remediation suggestions (ENG-3301).

review_comments: Marina Soto: Can we avoid breaking behavior for on-prem customers by default? Recommend audit mode default and an explicit opt-in to enforce.
Priya Natarajan (author): Agreed — defaulting to audit mode. Added helm flag and documented migration steps.
Evan Liu: Need stronger test coverage around policy precedence when multiple keys are referenced. Also validate race conditions during backfill.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added integration tests and a small mutex in the backfill script to avoid concurrent upgrades. Tests updated and run in CI.
Diego Alvarez: Audit log changes look good, but confirm downstream log-indexer schema compatibility.

notes_for_ops: Rollout steps: 1) Upgrade Private installer with default audit mode and backfill enabled; 2) Run backfill script and review generated report for non-compliant keys; 3) After remediation, switch privateInstaller.rbacV2.kmsResidency.mode to enforce during maintenance window.
Backfill script path: private-installer/scripts/kms_residency_backfill.sh. It writes a report to /var/lib/redwood/kms_residency_report.json on the target host.
Monitoring: added observability/dashboards/kms_residency.json for violations. Ops should create alerts on >10 violations/hour during transition.
Rollout window: recommended 2-week audit period before enforcement for large fleets.
